number_of_offences: Offences punishable u/ss 408, 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC were charged; three of the offences were finally upheld as triable only by Court of Session
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that no case was pending against the appellant as on the date the amendment came into force, and that the Magistrate was duty-bound to commit the case to the Court of Session as three of the offences were triable only by the Court of Session.

legal_representation.accused: June Chaudhary, Sumeeta Chaudhari, Prabhat Kumar, Anshuman Ashok, Dr. Kailash Chand

investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed after the amendment came into force

appeal_history.trial_court: The trial court held that since no charge-sheet had been filed before the Magistrate as on the date the amendment came into force, the case was exclusively triable by the Court of Session.
appeal_history.high_court: The High Court dismissed the revision petition filed by the appellant.
appeal_history.supreme_court: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, holding that the amendment was prospective and applied only to offences committed after the amendment came into force.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure made offences punishable under Sections 467, 468 and 471 IPC triable only by the Court of Sessions, and that since no case had been instituted against the appellant as of the amendment's effective date, the Magistrate was duty-bound to commit the case to the Court of Sessions.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant had acquired the right of trial by a forum specified in Schedule I of the 1973 Code, and that any amendment shifting the forum of trial to the Court of Sessions was not applicable to the appellant's case, as the case was pending before the Magistrate when the amendment came into force.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle that amendments to procedural law operate retrospectively unless the amendment explicitly states otherwise, and that the institution of a case is determined by the competent court taking cognizance of the offence.
